text: Feynman — Quantum Electrodynamics — Authoritative Textbook Reference (Quantum Field Theory, 106 pages). The feynman diagram is defined as a foundational theoretical formulation in Feynman — Quantum Electrodynamics governing quantum field theory. The Klein-Gordon equation governs relativistic spinless scalar fields satisfying the relativistic energy-momentum dispersion relation. The Dirac equation describes relativistic spin-half fermion fields and predicts the existence of antimatter positrons. Wick’s theorem relates time-ordered products of free quantum fields to sums of normal-ordered products and Feynman propagators. Goldstone’s theorem states that spontaneous breaking of a continuous global symmetry generates massless Nambu-Goldstone bosons. Core concepts and formulations in Feynman — Quantum Electrodynamics: feynman diagram, propagator, dirac equation, klein-gordon equation, renormalization, gauge invariance, wick theorem, dysons series.
